notes: Step 1 parts were correct: 1 Leonardo, 1 breadboard, 5 pushbuttons, 5 10k resistors and 12 jumper wires. Nothing was added or dropped.

Breadboard naming: the half of the board nearest the top rails is bank 't' (rows a-e, row e next to the centre gap). The lower half is bank 'b' (rows f-j, row f next to the gap). The picture's own row letters run the other way. This is only a naming choice and does not change the connectivity.
Rails: 'tp' is the top + rail and 'bn' is the bottom - (ground) rail. The hole numbers on the rails are only placeholders, because each rail is one strip.
Each button straddles the centre gap, with side 1 (1.l, 1.r) in the top half and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) in the bottom half. The legs sit in columns 6/8, 11/13, 16/18, 21/23 and 26/28, read from the image.

5V goes through a red wire to the + rail, then through a red wire to the top side of each button. The input pin (6, 5, 4, 3, 2) goes through a blue wire to the bottom side of that button. The 10k pull-down resistor runs from that same bottom column to the ground rail. The black wire joins Leonardo GND to the ground rail.
Pins 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2 go to buttons 1 to 5 in order, as in the image and schematic. The direction each button controls is not named in the manual.
The Leonardo's GND is taken as GND.1, the first GND pin next to 5V in the image.
